name: Juvenile Myasthenia Gravis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Juvenile Myasthenia Gravis

criteria.description: Presence of fluctuating skeletal muscle weakness with fatigability
Detection of acetylcholine receptor (AChR) or muscle-specific kinase (MuSK) antibodies
Abnormal repetitive nerve stimulation or single-fiber electromyography consistent with neuromuscular junction disorder
Improvement of symptoms with anticholinesterase agents or immunotherapy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of fluctuating muscle weakness plus either positive antibody testing or electrophysiological evidence of neuromuscular transmission defect
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be supported by response to treatment and exclusion of other neuromuscular disorders.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Fluctuating diplopia due to extraocular muscle weakness
searchTerms: double vision that changes due to eye muscle weakness
fluctuating diplopia from weak eye muscles
variable double vision caused by muscle fatigue
muscle weakness that worsens with activity

common.symptomName: Dysarthria due to bulbar muscle weakness
searchTerms: slurred speech from weak throat muscles
difficulty talking due to bulbar weakness
weakness in upper arm and thigh muscles
breathing difficulty from weak respiratory muscles
shortness of breath due to muscle weakness
slight loss of muscle bulk in arms or legs

rare.symptomName: Autonomic dysfunction including dry mouth or pupillary abnormalities
searchTerms: autonomic nervous system problems like dry mouth or pupil changes
enlarged thymus gland or tumor found

rare.symptomName: Severe myasthenic crisis requiring ventilatory support
searchTerms: severe muscle weakness crisis needing breathing support

laboratory: Presence of serum acetylcholine receptor antibodies
Presence of muscle-specific kinase (MuSK) antibodies in seronegative cases
imaging: Chest CT or MRI showing thymic hyperplasia or thymoma
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation; autoimmune etiology predominant
other: Electrophysiological studies showing decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation

distinguishingFeatures: Symptoms present from birth or early infancy

redFlags: Bulbar muscle weakness causing aspiration risk
Lack of response to anticholinesterase therapy
references: Gilhus NE. Myasthenia Gravis. N Engl J Med. 2016;375(26):2570-2581.
